title: fix: stop map gates and telemetry opt-outs from failing silently

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+---
+'@evlog/cli': patch
+---
+
+Every command now stops on a flag it does not declare, and on a value flag passed with no value, with exit code 2. `evlog map --min-scor 90` used to run with no gate and exit 0, and `evlog init --dryrun` wrote files. A flag written before the command name is checked too: `evlog --dry-run init` used to run `init` for real. A script that carries a mistyped flag today starts failing: fix the spelling.
+
+The other usage errors exit 2 as well, as the README documents: an unknown command, an invalid `--min-score`, `--framework`, `--format` or `--limit`, and `evlog map <entry>` for an entry point that does not exist. An empty `--min-score`, which is what an unset shell variable expands to, is one of them. A bare `--baseline` no longer takes the flag after it as its value: `evlog map --baseline --min-score 80` and `evlog map --baseline --cwd apps/web` read both flags. A `map` error is printed as JSON under `--format json`, as it already was under `--json`.

@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+---
+'@evlog/cli': patch
+---
+
+`evlog map` no longer scores a tree it only partly read.
+
+- A file with a syntax error, or one the scan cannot read, used to lose its routes, which raised the score. The report now warns `<file> failed to parse` and counts the file as one failing entry point. With `--min-score`, `map.minScore` or `--baseline`, the run stops with `cli.MAP_PARSE_FAILED`, exits 1, and leaves `evlog.map.json` as it was. List the file under `map.ignore` when it is not app code.
+- Directories named `build`, `dist` and `coverage` are skipped at the project root only, so `server/api/build/index.get.ts` is scanned.
+- Two entry points with the same method and path, such as `get('/')` in two routers, get distinct ids. `--baseline` reported regressions on an unchanged tree when they shared one. The id of every other entry point is unchanged, so a committed map stays comparable, and an entry point is still compared with itself when a second one with its method and path appears or goes. If it also moved to another file in that change, it is compared with the entry point that has its method and path and lost the most checks, then the lowest-scoring one.
+- `.js`, `.mjs` and `.cjs` files are parsed with JSX, so a Next.js `page.js` is checked instead of reported as `n/a`.
+
+The first and the last of these can change a verdict on code you did not touch, so the rule-set version moves to 2. `--baseline` against a map written by an earlier CLI exits 2 with the version mismatch: run `evlog map` once and commit the new `evlog.map.json`.

@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
+---
+'@evlog/telemetry': patch
+'@evlog/cli': patch
+---
+
+New `telemetry.fail(code?)` for a command that handles its own failure: it prints the error, sets an exit code and returns, so the run used to be recorded as `outcome: "success"`. Call it where the error is handled and the event carries `outcome: "error"` with `code` as its `errorCode`.
+
+The evlog CLI calls it for every error it reports, so `evlog logs` with no log directory, `evlog config` on an invalid file and a mistyped flag are sent as errors with their `cli.*` code. A failed `--min-score` or `--baseline` gate stays a successful run with `mapGateFailed: true`.

@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@
+---
+'@evlog/telemetry': patch
+'@evlog/cli': patch
+---
+
+Telemetry now does what its docs say.
+
+- The run that opts out is no longer queued: `telemetry disable`, or `disableTelemetry()` called inside a run, used to purge the outbox and then write its own event to it. `disableTelemetry()` turns off every handle created for the tool, and a `flush()` already sending stops at the batch in flight.
+- `EVLOG_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=1` prints each run's event as the run ends and makes no request. The event is not queued either. It used to print at the next flush, and that flush sent the events.
+- An endpoint that never answers no longer keeps the process alive for ten seconds. The drain closes its connection at the 400 ms timeout. It no longer follows redirects, so `endpoint` has to be the final URL.
+- `DO_NOT_TRACK=true`, `yes` and `on` opt out like `1`, and `EVLOG_TELEMETRY=false`, `no` and `off` like `0`.
+- `withTelemetry()` records only the flags a command declares. An undeclared flag used to be sent by name, and a positional as `<set>`.
+- New `bin` option: the command people type, when it is not `name`. The first-run notice prints `<bin> telemetry disable`, so the evlog CLI's notice now says `evlog telemetry disable`, not `evlog-cli telemetry disable`.
+- `evlog telemetry status` lists the allowlisted `init*`, `map*` and `logs*` values. The fields `evlog logs` records are documented.

@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+import type { ArgsDef } from 'citty'
+import { cliErrors } from './errors'
+
+function camelCase(name: string): string {
+  return name.replace(/-([a-z0-9])/gi, (_, char: string) => char.toUpperCase())
+}
+
+function looksLikeFlag(arg: string): boolean {
+  return /^--|^-[a-z]/i.test(arg)
+}
+
+/**
+ * Check `rawArgs` against the flags a command declares, and return them ready
+ * for citty to parse.
+ *
+ * citty parses leniently: a flag it does not know becomes a boolean with its
+ * value left behind as a positional, and a value flag with nothing after it
+ * reads as unset. Both let a mistyped gate run the command without the gate, so
+ * both are refused here.
+ *
+ * @param bare - Value flags that also work alone, like `--baseline`. One that
+ * is last or followed by another flag is rewritten to `--flag=`, which keeps
+ * citty from reading the next flag as its value.
+ * @throws `cli.UNKNOWN_FLAG` or `cli.FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE`.
+ */
+export function checkFlags(rawArgs: readonly string[], args: ArgsDef, bare: readonly string[] = []): string[] {
+  const declared = new Map<string, { key: string, takesValue: boolean }>()
+  for (const [key, def] of Object.entries(args)) {
+    if (def.type === 'positional') continue
+    const flag = { key, takesValue: def.type === 'string' || def.type === 'enum' }
+    declared.set(key, flag)
+    for (const alias of 'alias' in def ? [def.alias ?? []].flat() : []) declared.set(alias, flag)
+  }
+  const find = (name: string) => declared.get(name) ?? declared.get(camelCase(name))
+
+  const end = rawArgs.indexOf('--')

+import { runCommand } from 'citty'
+import type { ArgsDef, CommandDef, Resolvable } from 'citty'
+import { EvlogError } from 'evlog'
+import { EXIT_FAIL, EXIT_USAGE, setExitCode, writeHuman, writeStdout } from './core/output'
+import { resolve, resolveCommand, showUsage } from './core/usage'
+import { VERSION } from './lib/constants'
+import { isUsageError } from './lib/errors'
+import { checkFlags } from './lib/flags'
+import { main } from './index'
+
+/**
+ * Check the flags written before a subcommand's name against the command they
+ * were given to, down to the leaf, which checks its own.
+ *
+ * citty hands a subcommand only what follows its name, so nothing else reads
+ * the flag in `evlog --dry-run init`, and `init` would run for real.
+ */
+async function checkGroupFlags(cmd: CommandDef<any>, rawArgs: string[]): Promise<void> {
+  const subCommands = await resolve(cmd.subCommands)
+  if (!subCommands || Object.keys(subCommands).length === 0) return
+  const index = rawArgs.findIndex(arg => !arg.startsWith('-'))
+  checkFlags(index === -1 ? rawArgs : rawArgs.slice(0, index), await resolve(cmd.args as ArgsDef | undefined) ?? {})
+  const sub = index === -1 ? undefined : subCommands[rawArgs[index]!]
+  if (sub) await checkGroupFlags(await resolve(sub as Resolvable<CommandDef<any>>) as CommandDef<any>, rawArgs.slice(index + 1))
+}
+
+/**
+ * Run the CLI on `rawArgs` and set the exit code.
+ *
+ * In place of citty's `runMain`, which exits 1 whatever went wrong: an unknown
+ * command, or a group called without a subcommand, is a usage error and exits 2
+ * like an unknown flag does.
+ */
+export async function run(rawArgs: string[]): Promise<void> {
+  if (rawArgs.includes('--help') || rawArgs.includes('-h')) {
+    await showUsage(...await resolveCommand(main, rawArgs))
+    return
+  }
+  if (rawArgs.length === 1 && (rawArgs[0] === '--version' || rawArgs[0] === '-v')) {
+    writeStdout(VERSION)
+    return
+  }
+
+  try {
+    await checkGroupFlags(main, rawArgs)
+    await runCommand(main, { rawArgs })
+  } catch (error) {
+    if (error instanceof EvlogError && isUsageError(error)) {
+      writeHuman(error.fix ? `${error.message}\n→ ${error.fix}` : error.message)
+      setExitCode(EXIT_USAGE)
+      return
+    }
+    if (error instanceof Error && error.name === 'CLIError') {
+      await showUsage(...await resolveCommand(main, rawArgs))
+      writeHuman(error.message)
+      setExitCode(EXIT_USAGE)
+      return
+    }
+    console.error(error, '\n')
+    setExitCode(EXIT_FAIL)
+  }
+}
